after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of a data set ${x}_{i}$ consisting of $5$ data points, where 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i}=-20,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i}^{2}=170.
$$
after.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i}=-20,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-20) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i}^{2}=170,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 170 \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =34-{(-4)}^{2} \\  & =34-16 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

If we have a data set that consists of the points x1,x2,…,xn, then the variance can be computed as σ2=x2―−(x―)2,

where x― is the mean of the data set and x2― is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute x―. There are n=5 points in our data set, and we know that ∑i=15xi=−20, so we get

x―=1n∑i=1nxi=15∑i=15xi=15⋅(−20)=−4.

Now, let's compute x2―. We know that ∑i=15xi2=170, so we get

x2―=1n∑i=1nxi2=15∑i=15xi2=15⋅170=34.

So, the variance is

σ2=x2―−(x―)2=34−(−4)2=34−16=18.

after.problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of a data set ${x}_{i}$ consisting of $7$ data points, where

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}=35,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}^{2}=201.
$$
after.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}=35,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 35 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}^{2}=201,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 201 \\  & =\frac{201}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{201}{7}-{(5)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{201}{7}-25 \\  & =\frac{201-175}{7} \\  & =\frac{26}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

If we have a data set that consists of the points x1,x2,…,xn, then the variance of the data set is given by σ2=x2―−(x―)2,

where x― is the mean of the data set and x2― is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute x―. There are n=7 points in our data set, and we know that ∑i=17xi=35, so we get

x―=1n∑i=1nxi=17∑i=17xi=17⋅35=5.

Now, let's compute x2―. We know that ∑i=17xi2=201, so we get

x2―=1n∑i=1nxi2=17∑i=17xi2=17⋅201=2017.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance Given the Number, Sum, and Sum of Squares of the Data Points
content.problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of a data set ${x}_{i}$ consisting of $7$ data points, where

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}=35,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}^{2}=201.
$$
content.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}=35,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 35 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}^{2}=201,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}{\sum }_{i=1}^{7}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 201 \\  & =\frac{201}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{201}{7}-{(5)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{201}{7}-25 \\  & =\frac{201-175}{7} \\  & =\frac{26}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Compute the standard deviation $\sigma $ of the following data set:

$$
10,\,14,\,16,\,9,\,12,\,5
$$

Do not round your answer.

$\sigma =$
{{field-1}}
after.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=6$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (10+14+16+9+12+5) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 66 \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot [{10}^{2}+{14}^{2}+{16}^{2}+{9}^{2}+{12}^{2}+{5}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot [100+196+256+81+144+25] \\  & =\frac{802}{6} \\  & =\frac{401}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{401}{3}-{(11)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{401}{3}-121 \\  & =\frac{401-363}{3} \\  & =\frac{38}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{38}{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
